strengths: Pedestrian signal obedience as Road Traffic Act, not ‘just manners,’ is the right legal frame.
No invented yen fines or survey percentages.
Enforcement hedged as possible fines vs anecdote of warnings.
Jaywalking FAQ refuses to collapse unsignaled crossing into one English penalty.
verified: Road Traffic Act requires pedestrians to obey traffic signals.
Elementary traffic-safety lessons and 横断歩道 practice are ordinary, not a unique national curriculum quote.
Flashing pedestrian green is taught as a warning that red is coming.
questionable: Pole/station cameras as a reason people wait: being observed is real; camera ticketing of pedestrians is over-read if stated as a common device.
needs_source: If any future draft names a fine amount or campaign year, it needs a cited ordinance/notice—do not invent one now.

issues.location: Empty Streets / Learn to Stop — cameras
issues.problem: Camera-on-the-pole as a waiting cause mixes security CCTV with implied automated enforcement.
issues.suggestion: Hedge: some people mention cameras; everyday pressure is other pedestrians, school zones, and occasional officers. No fake enforcement stats.

issues.location: What the Law Actually Says — ‘fines can apply’
issues.problem: True but unspecified; readers hunting a number may fill one in.
